svg.title: TOPAK B6 — The trust anchor is a havoc issuer, and its custody is a declaration
svg.desc: Promotion moves the gate up one level: the authority that defines who votes cannot itself be voted in without regress. ADR-0025 makes that authority a havoc issuer, splits "infallible" three ways, and declares custody per rung as a pair (capture threshold, loss tolerance) that never enters a proof.
svg.text: TOPAK · B6

text.tspan: The trust anchor is a havoc issuer, and its custody is a declaration

svg.text: Promotion moves the gate up one level: the authority that defines who votes cannot itself be voted in without regress. ADR-0025 makes that authority a havoc issuer, splits "infallible" three ways, and declares custody per rung as a pair (capture threshold, loss tolerance) that never enters a proof.

text.tspan: Three treatments were weighed (ADR-0025 Context, Options)
Havoc, with "infallible" split three ways (ADR-0025 §2; ToO §7.2)

svg.text: Rejected. Key theft becomes infallible too; the rules floor loses its justification; silent degradation escapes declaration; P1 is
abandoned at the top of the authority chain; residual risk and GOVERN 2.3 accountability become unstatable.
Chosen. Safety is proven for every issuance the anchor could make, so its composition never enters the proof.
Rejected. Adds governance content, not proof content; every custody change would couple to re-verification.
Rejected. Relocates the axiom without removing it.
ASSUMED, the sole axiom
An authentic issuance at the current anchor epoch is what the anchor intended.
Above every proof: no safety theorem covers it
MODELED under havoc
Issue is an environment action, constrained only by Authentic, epoch increment and the rules floor (ADR-0026). Safety is proven for every issuance sequence
satisfying those constraints.
Inside the specification and the verified object.
Discharged as written since 2026.10.02:
Anchor_proof.tla proves FloorPreserved for
every floor subset and epoch bound (ADR-0046;
ADR-0029 B25), of the module
DECLARED per rung (ADR-0023)
The pair (capture threshold, loss tolerance), plus the composition and eviction rules that make it true. Not in the model.
A declaration record; changing it never reopens
Constrained only by Authentic(i), an epoch increment and the rules floor.
Authentic(i) is opaque in the specification.
An admitted issuance voids in-flight votes at the new rules epoch (ADR-0024 §3), and is
persisted with genesis residency (ADR-0027 §3).
Bounds every issuance: a havoc issuer with no floor could set a roster of one.
The quorum's archetype values live here, so a promotion degeneracy is a
mechanism release and reopens the promotion theorem (ADR-0024).
Changing the floor needs two keys: an issuance plus a promotion (ADR-0026 §4).

text.tspan: Modeled · inside the specification and the verified object

svg.text: Which keys, and how many signatures: the declaration instantiates Authentic.
Plus the composition and eviction rules that make the pair true.
A custody degeneracy is a declaration and reopens nothing.
The two axes, approver fault tolerance and anchor recoverability, are declared independently.

text.tspan: Declared · outside the model, per rung

svg.text: instantiates Authentic
An authentic issuance at the current anchor epoch is what the anchor
intended.
The authority regress ends here (ToO §7.6): ADR-0002 a declared
axiom set; ADR-0010 a verified artifact; ADR-0025 with ADR-0026 one
axiom, bounded by two verified floors.

text.tspan: Custody is a declaration axis: anchor recoverability (ADR-0025 Annex; ToO §7.2)

svg.text: Archetype · strict unanimity
n−1 eviction with replacement
TUF-style threshold with recovery
Genesis custody today (ADR-0029 §1)
Order is position on the axis, not record number: "record numbers follow drafting order; position on the axis does not." Every pair is (capture threshold, loss tolerance).
Strict unanimity, n ≥ 3
n−1 eviction with replacement
Threshold with recovery, in the shape of The Update Framework (TUF) root role
Single custodian
— (the archetype)
No key-holder is removed without their own consent
Rule changes carry unanimous consent
Signed by every key in the anchor key set at the current epoch
Unanimity of the remaining n−1 evicts one key-holder, atomically with seating a replacement
k of n signatures; a genesis-declared recovery rule lets k rotate any key
Unanimous quorum of Mediated key-holders, n ≥ 3
One eviction per anchor epoch; n ≥ 3; the replacement countersigns
One person: Scott (ADR-0029 §1)
At the gate (ADR-0002 A2): removable only with their own consent. Mediated applies as an attribution
predicate only
Principals. The gate moves to the genesis-declared eviction rule
Principals. The gate moves to the genesis threshold-and-recovery rule
Any permanent loss freezes the rules: the system can run and subtract, but cannot change
Freeze requires a second loss within one replacement window
Liveness under up to n−k losses
A permanent loss, therefore a freeze. Unanimity leaves no rule to seat a replacement; to leave without
freezing, first move the deployment to D-0025-2
The eviction rule run with the departing key-holder's consent; consumes the epoch's one eviction, so
a resignation and a compromise cannot be handled in the same anchor epoch
Absorbed by the recovery rule: k rotate the resigning key. No freeze while k remain; dropping below k
is a loss like any other
— (the archetype is the reference point)
A compromised key-holder's permanent veto ends
Liveness under up to n−k losses
Consent to one's own removal
A k-coalition can issue rules over n−k objections
Re-genesis: a successor system, not a continuation
Optional: a time-locked notice window in which an outside quorum may deny (subtractive, so admissible)
Prior art: TUF root role and root-key rotation; RFC 6024

The annex entries are declaration records under ADR-0023, separately supersedable, and not decision clauses of ADR-0025; they ratified with it in Batch 2 as declarations. The single custodian appears only as an axis position: its pair is (1, 0), and the annex writes no row for it.

text.tspan: Who is at the gate, per custody (ToO §7.5)

svg.text: Archetype custody: key-holders are removable only with their own consent, so they sit at the gate
(B14): attributable non-principals, Mediated as attribution only.
Degenerate custody: the eviction or threshold rule can remove a key-holder, so key-holders become
principals and the gate moves to that rule. That is a type change, and it moves the TCB (§8.2); it
voids no theorem, so it is declared and checked (ADR-0023).
Promotion voters are principals on every rung, because the anchor can evict them.
At A-0025, a permanent loss (or a resignation) freezes the rules.
Frozen: the system runs and subtracts, but cannot change; anchor unavailability blocks change, never
operation (ADR-0027 §3).
The only exit is re-genesis: a successor system and a new rules-epoch chain (ADR-0027 §4).
That fragility pushes operators toward degenerate custody, which is correct as long as it is declared.
Re-genesis migration is open (G7 item 10): what a successor inherits, including read access to the
forensic classes, whose horizon is the epoch chain (ADR-0028 §3).

text.tspan: A coalition at the capture threshold can issue any rules-floor-conformant roster.

svg.text: No safety theorem covers anchor intent. The rules floor bounds what it can issue; nothing bounds why.
The residual becomes numeric: the capture threshold feeds NIST MANAGE 1.4.
Trusted-base rows (ADR-0045, in force, C2/C4): T-0045-8 the anchor key store, T-0045-9 the
key-holders "honest at the declared capture threshold", both trust roots.
Genesis custody: Scott, sole custodian, (1, 0) (ADR-0029 §1; G7 header). Genesis, not a degeneracy:
there is no archetype custody before the anchor exists.
The corpus's own row is T-0045-11, now in force; the dev bundle key is a second (1, 0) custody (G7
A solo bootstrap is not a bootstrap. The ceremony seats key-holders under a declared custody record
(ADR-0029 §5); the archetype needs three (A-0025) of the five humans.
Owed: the genesis key-ceremony procedure, and a named owner and role for every custody declaration
(GOVERN 2.3).

Status: ADR-0025 is Accepted (genesis), 2026.09.23 (Batch 2), A1 ratified 2026.09.30 (Batch 17), with no confirmation marker: a bootstrap record (ADR-0029 §4). A1 added item (f), the keys that vouch for artifacts; its schema fields exist in the reference since ADR-0033 A6 (B23).

ADR-0029 B25; boundary register B14
